title: CLIP goes 3D: Leveraging Prompt Tuning for Language Grounded 3D Recognition
role: A template for training a new encoder beside a frozen CLIP; it involves no noise, no sampler and no gradient into a picture.
reads: Clean point clouds through a 3D encoder, clean rendered views through CLIP's image encoder with learned prompts, and template captions through CLIP's text encoder.
trained_on: ShapeNet, 52,460 CAD models in 55 categories, as point cloud, render and template caption triplets; InfoNCE with same-class positives; only the 3D encoder and visual prompts train.
score_enters: No gradient enters a sampler: the similarity score is used only for zero-shot classification and retrieval.
unseen: partly: zero-shot tests on other datasets, called unseen, with no step removing categories shared with ShapeNet.
headline: Zero-shot classification accuracy on ModelNet40 is 50.6% for PointTransformer with CG3D against 20.2% for PointCLIP, and 25.6% against 15.4% on real scans in ScanObjectNN.
copy_or_avoid: Copy the two-way contrastive loss to a frozen CLIP; avoid class-level positives and single-object captions for binding and word-order pairs (inferred).
model: CLIP (SLIP ViT-Base) with PointTransformer or PointMLP, no diffusion model

disagreements.paper_says: Training uses all 55 ShapeNet categories and no removal of shared categories is described; everyday classes such as chair and table occur in both (inferred).
Table 4 gives PointCLIP 10.1% on ModelNet40, described in the text as single-view.
